Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:29: Indeed, the building of the soul is from the side of Chesed, which is the daughter of Abraham our father, as Rashbi explains (Mishpatim 95a); and therefore Abraham our father, peace be upon him, merited Chesed, because he did not have pity on his body or his wealth - for by nature it is hard for a person to give over his soul and body for the sanctification of the [divine] Name, which is contrary to nature, and the flesh opposes it. And so too, giving one's wealth to charity, especially if he distributes much and acts contrary to nature, binds him to Chesed. And from this the discerning reader may infer, for all the other matters of divine service that are contrary to nature, that one must do them out of love in order to merit Chesed - and this is the matter of the ten trials with which Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was tested, as explained in the discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:30: And what they said, that "everlasting love" is that the lower world binds to the upper world without separation, and it says at the end, "blessed be He forever and ever" - it seems to me that the general sense of these words may be understood together with what is explained in the Tikkunim (new section, page 100b), which I have in manuscript, in these words: the Sava arose and took a stone in his hands, opened and said: holy lamp, until now you were a stone in your hand; from now on, behold, you have ascended among the supernal ones - guard yourself from her stones. For in the mouths of the righteous she ascends, through their prayers to her husband and through their deeds; for this stone, when it descends below, is a "touchstone" [concerning which it is said (Psalms 11:5), "the LORD tests the righteous"], and through it the fathers were tested; and therefore it is said (ibid. 118:22), "the stone which the builders rejected" - these are the fathers - and when it descends below, it descends in this configuration, "David" [an anagram referencing the letters of the Name]; and when it ascends, it is said of it, "the stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone" - in this configuration, YHVH. Through it Abraham was tested with ten trials, and at the time a person is tested through it, it is lowered; and after he stands firm in his trial, it ascends through him to its husband, who is YHVH - at that time the person ascends through it above all those levels and officers through which a person is tested. And when Samael saw that permission was given over every righteous man to be a trial for him, and he saw that he stood firm in his standing, he said, "and all this avails me nothing" - and should you say this was said by Haman concerning Mordechai, certainly Haman was an embodiment of Samael, in whom he was clothed, and the ten lower crowns were clothed in his ten sons. And because he [Abraham] stood firm in the trial, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave it into his hand - how much more so one who is tested for the sake of the Shechinah in exile, because ten treasures of the Name of the crown descend upon her - which are Y-H-V-H, sefirot full of treasures that surround the supernal crown of the King and the Matronita - and this is the supernal crown of which it is said, on the holy day of Shabbat, in the Kedushah, "a crown they shall give to You, O LORD our God" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:31: Further, the matter of love is explained (Zohar, Ki Tisa, page 190b), in these words: the Torah has love, brotherhood, and truth in it. Abraham loved Isaac; Isaac loved Abraham - they embrace one another. Jacob - both of them hold onto him with love and brotherhood, giving him their spirit, one to the other.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:32: Rashbi, peace be upon him, taught us the secret of the nature of love, and the matter is [understood] through what he said above this, concerning the matter of the love between colleagues: "all the colleagues in Rabbi Shimon's days had between them a love of soul and spirit." And this matter is clear, for a person's love for his fellow comes through the soul, for the will of the soul is love; and although bodies are divided and separated from one another, the soul of this one and that one is spiritual, and spirituality is not separated but unified in the ultimate unity - and when the soul of one colleague arouses its will to love his fellow, his fellow's soul is also aroused and loves him, and the two souls become one - as the verse says concerning David and Jonathan (I Samuel 18:1), "and the soul of Jonathan was bound with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul"; and David's love for Jonathan is shown by his love for him, as it says (ibid. 20:41), "and they kissed one another and wept," and so on, "until David exceeded" [in weeping] - and so he said at his death (II Samuel 1:26), "your love to me was wonderful, surpassing the love of women."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:33: And the reality that souls bind to one another through the arousal of love, King Solomon, peace be upon him, taught us, when he said (Proverbs 27:19), "as face answers to face in water, so the heart of man to man." And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Yalkut 961): Rabbi Chanina said, do waters have a face? Rather, just as you place these waters in a vessel and gaze into them and they appear to you, so is the heart of man to man - to this point. And this is explained by what they explain there: just as the waters in a vessel, when a person gazes into them, he sees his own face in them - and there are two kinds of "faces": the first, the face he gazes with, which is direct light, and the face in the water, which he sees as reflected light returning from below, from the water in the vessel, upward to him - and the two faces are one, bound together as one; and if the person removes his gaze from the water, nothing at all will appear in the water, for if there is no direct light, there is no reflected light. So it is with "the heart of man to man" - when a person arouses the will of his heart to love his fellow, that will arouses the will of his fellow's heart toward him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:34: And although we said that the face a person gazes at in the water is direct light - this is according to physical reality; but in spiritual reality, this is the secret of the arousal from below, which rises from our deeds to the Shechinah - and this is the matter of "female waters" [mayin nukvin] mentioned in the Zohar (Bereshit 18a); and if there is no arousal from below, there is no arousal from above, as it is said (Genesis 2:6), "and a mist went up from the earth," and afterward, "and watered" - as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (35a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:35: And to understand the words of the parable regarding the allegory in all their particulars: just as, for a person to gaze into water so that his face appears there, two things are needed - water and a vessel - and if either of these is lacking, no face will appear at all - so too, a soul and a heart are needed. And it has already been explained in the Tikkunim, in several places (70b), that the soul dwells in the heart - the heart is the vessel and the soul is the water in the vessel, so that a heart without a soul is like a vessel without water. And just as, in gazing at water, if there is no vessel nothing will appear - for the vessel, because it is opaque, is the cause that makes that form return backward, since the water is transparent, and because of its transparency the form appearing in it passes through and out of it if there is nothing to stop the form - it is like the parable of a polished mirror: if there is no opaque backing behind it to stop the form, the form will pass out through it and the person will see nothing - so a person will not acquire love in the soul of a person he has not seen the form of that person, so that, when his love for him is aroused, his fellow's love for him will be aroused; and the gazing of faces in the water is the arousal of love that is aroused from the will of the soul in his heart toward the soul in his fellow's heart, and then the two souls bind together in one bond of love, even though they may be distant from one another - for the waters, which are the souls, are fine and spiritual, all a portion of God from above, and there is no separation between them, even though they are in separate vessels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:36: And it is like the parable of the inner essence of the Divine, which is within the vessel of sapphire, where the inner essence is entirely one, unified, even though the vessels change; and you already know that in the Ra'aya Meheimna (end of Bo, 42b) the inner essence is likened to water that spreads within vessels, such that if the vessels break, the water returns to its source, and they all become one source, as they were before spreading out. And the distinction of direct light and reflected light, which are "face to face," I will not explain here, since I rely on what has already been explained by my teacher, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:37: And now, with this introduction, we may understand what the discourse says - "with love and brotherhood they give him their spirit, one to the other" - for the binding of the attributes to one another in this love is through their inner spirit, for from the side of the vessels they are separate vessels in their function - this one Chesed, this one judgment, this one mercy - but through the spirit, which is one, as it is written (cf. Ecclesiastes 3:19), "and they all have one spirit," they bind together and "give him their spirit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:38: And incidentally, we learn from the parable "as face answers to face in water" that it is impossible for a person, when he wishes to cleave to his Creator in the secret of love, to cleave to Him in His aspect prior to Atzilut - for that aspect of His is hidden and has no grasp of love in it, similar to the parable we made, that a person cannot love a soul in the abstract, without the form of a body, even though there is no [literal] body above, Heaven forfend - the intent is toward the reality of the revelation of His actions to us, similar to the soul that reveals its actions, but before it is clothed in a body it has no action. And so they explain (Ra'aya Meheimna, there), in these words: before He created an image in the world and formed a form, He was singular, without form or likeness; and whoever recognizes Him as He was before creation, who is beyond image, is forbidden to make Him a form and an image in the world - neither with the letter hei, nor with the letter yud, and not even with the holy Name, nor with any letter or point in the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:39: And if a person cleaves his soul, it is in the secret of the supernal life that spreads within the vessels, which are His holy names - and this is (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to YHVH your God are all alive today" - meaning, they are bound to the eternal Living One, blessed be He, who is bound to His Name, and He and His Name are entirely one - YHVH is His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:40: And when a person cleaves to his Creator in complete love, with heart and with soul, he thereby causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to cleave to him, similar to the "faces in water" I explained. And so Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Terumah, page 162a), in these words: "and you shall love" - this is the beginning of the right side, to love the Holy One, blessed be He, with love of cleaving to Him. And who is this "right side" that arouses love? Whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, arouses His right side toward him and He receives him with love. All matters of the world depend only on will; spirit draws spirit and brings spirit - and the sign of this is (Job 34:14), "if He should set His heart upon him, He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul." When a person arouses love toward the Holy One, blessed be He, the arousal of the right side is aroused only through three aspects, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:5), "with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might" - behold, three aspects here, lest you say "either this or that" - for it is not written "either with all your heart, or with all your soul, or with all your might," but rather all of them are needed: heart, soul, and money. And then the Holy One, blessed be He, arouses His right side toward him and extends it to meet him and receives him - and of this it is written (Psalms 110:1), "the LORD said to my lord, sit at My right hand" - and the secret of this verse, we have already discussed, is that King David spoke of his own level, when he was bound to the right side - to this point. And our intent in this discourse is explained: that it says that when a person gives over his spirit to love the [divine] Name, he thereby causes the Name to love him and cleave to him - and this is what it means by "spirit draws spirit and brings spirit" - the intent being that when a person arouses his spirit toward the Name, so the spirit of the Name will be drawn to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:41: And along these lines, Rabbi Yosi himself, the author of this discourse, explains in Parashat Korach, on the verse (Job 34:14), "if He should set His heart upon him, He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul" - that the intent is toward one who performs levirate marriage with his brother's wife: "if He should set His heart upon him" means toward the soul of his brother, to bring there his heart, meaning his intention; "He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul" - with his good intention he draws the soul of the deceased and is built up through him; and if not, he is not built up. In these words of Rashbi (Zohar, Korach 177a): "if He should set His heart upon him" - this person who is charged to build up the building [through levirate marriage] must direct his heart and his will toward that deceased one. From here, one who comes upon that woman for the sake of her beauty and desire for her - behold, the building of the world is not built, for the will and the heart are not directed toward the deceased; and therefore it is written, "if He should set His heart upon him," with the will of the heart directed toward him - then "He would gather to Himself his spirit and his soul," and it is drawn to him - to the extent relevant here. Behold, it is explicit that the spirit of the living and his intention draws another spirit in this world; and correspondingly, concerning the matter of intention in love - when he sets his heart, his soul, and his money with the desire of love of his Creator, he thereby draws the supernal, divine spirit upon himself - namely, the Holy One, blessed be He, extends His right hand toward him and receives him. And the matter of "and receives him" will be explained to you in chapter 3, in the secret of the "kisses of lovers."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:42: Further, this matter of love is explained at the end of the words of the Sava (Mishpatim 114a), where Rabbi Chiya says, on the verse (Song of Songs 8:6), "set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm" - the matter of the love and binding of the Community of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He; and he says afterward: we have this love and the burning flames of the heart after You - may it be [His] will that our image be engraved on Your heart, just as Your image is engraved on our heart - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:43: And from this the discerning reader may distinguish the matter of the love of the LORD - for when a person engraves the image of the Name YHVH in his heart always, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 16:8), "I have set YHVH before me always," he thereby causes the image of his soul to be engraved above, and the Creator, blessed be He, will love him - and this is the matter of "as face answers to face in water" that I explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:44: And the end of the verse, "so the heart of man" - in the way of the secret, just as it is according to the plain sense I explained above, so is it exactly in its hint above: for when a person arouses his heart to love the LORD, he is called Adam [man] in the secret of yud-heh-vav-heh, which adds up to "Adam" [in gematria] - for YHVH will love him and bind to him, as it is written (I Chronicles 28:9), "if you seek Him, He will be found by you" - meaning that the arousal from below must always come first. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Pinchas 241a), concerning the matter of falling on one's face [tachanun], where he says: then Adam, who is the image that includes all the rest, lowers himself and prostrates on his face, and gives over his own being and spirit to Adam [the supernal configuration], who is engraved upon those images, to arouse Him concerning it as is fitting - and this is (Psalms 25:1), "to You, O LORD, I lift up my soul" - to this point. And when you examine his words, where he says "to arouse Him concerning it," you will find our words aligned with his - and from this we learn the secret of love for all other matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:45: Behold, it is explained in this chapter what the nature of the matter of love is: that its reality is the bond and unity of the caused things with one another through their inner soul; and so too, a person does not love the [divine] Name and cleave to Him except through his soul - namely, "with all your soul," as we shall explain - and this is the word "ahavah" [love] meaning "cleaving" [dvekut], as it says (Deuteronomy 30:20), "to love the LORD," and so on, "and to cleave to Him" - for through love one cleaves to Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 1:46: There are further particulars concerning the nature of the matter of love that will be explained in a chapter of their own, in order to give some breathing space between chapters:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:1: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Va'etchanan 267b) that all of Atzilut is called "ahavah" [love]; in these words: come and see, everything is called "love," and for the sake of love everything endures, as it is written (Song of Songs 8:7), "many waters cannot quench love," and everything endures through love - for the holy Name is found thus: for it has been established, the yud, its tip above, is never separated from the yud, for love rests upon it and it is never separated from it. As for the heh - it has been established that the yud is never separated from it, and they are found together in affection, never separated from one another, yud-heh; and this is stated, as it is written (Genesis 2:10), "and a river went out from Eden" - "went out" forever, in affection they cleave to one another. The vav is always the bridegroom to the bride, whose way is in affection - yud in heh, heh with vav, vav with heh - therefore everything is called "love," and one is bound to the other in affection; and therefore whoever loves the King is thereby bound in that love, and therefore, "and you shall love YHVH your God" - to this point. Behold, it explains explicitly that all of Atzilut is designated by the word "ahavah."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:2: And now there is a difficulty with what was explained in the previous chapter, that love, specifically, is designated for Chesed - and this is also explained above, in this same discourse we copied (267b): "and you shall love" - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with Chesed on every side.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:3: And in the Tikkunim (Zohar Chadash 101a), love is explained as belonging to Binah, and it appears that this is where its root is; in these words, concerning the matter of fear and love: correspondingly, one who fears the Holy One, blessed be He, the yud rests and enters his heart; and one who loves Him, the heh rests in his brain. And concerning these two letters it is said, "the hidden things" - for whether a person fears the Holy One, blessed be He, or loves Him, is hidden from other people; and "the revealed things" are vav and heh - one who occupies himself with Torah, the vav rests in his mouth; and one who occupies himself with a commandment, the heh rests in his 248 limbs - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:4: And in these words of his, fear is also explained (Zohar, Naso 122b): this is what is upon a person's head, and from it fear enters the heart of a person, to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and to guard himself from transgressing the negative commandments. The heh, love, is upon a person's head, and from it enters the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, upon his 248 limbs, to fulfill through them the positive commandments. The vav is upon a person's head, and from it enters the mouth of a person, words to teach Torah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:5: Indeed, what appears in reconciling these discourses is that there is a distinction between the reality of the love a person has for the Holy One, blessed be He, and the reality of love above, in Atzilut - for the reality of love in Atzilut is that all of Atzilut is called "love," since love means the bond and unity of the caused things with one another, as I explained in the previous chapter, and therefore all of Atzilut is unified in its parts in complete bond and unity, and therefore in it all, as one, love is rightly applied. But from where love is drawn to a person, Rashbi further explains to us: that from the side of the supernal heh, love will be drawn to him, to fulfill the commandments with desire - as we shall explain the reason.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:6: And after a person merits to be a lover of the King and fulfill the commandments with desire, which causes the bond and unity of the attributes, called "love" - then he merits the right side, called "love," as I explained in the previous chapter, that the reason it is called "love" is because of the bond of the left with the right. And so it is precise in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, when he says, "and you shall love" - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned with Chesed on every side - meaning, from every aspect of Chesed and its completeness; and the completeness of Chesed is the inclusion of Gevurah within it, and a person merits it only by giving over his body, soul, and wealth in love of his Creator, like Abraham.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:7: And what causes Chesed and judgment to bind together certainly also causes all the attributes to bind together as one; and although it is said that the lover merits the right side, the intent is not to the right arm alone, but rather he merits all the attributes together, since they are all flowed from Chesed, and from the side of Chesed the ten sefirot are unified, as we say (Sotah 47a), "the right draws near," and "let bone approach its bone" (Ezekiel 37:7) - and they explain this verse in the Tikkunim (105b) as referring to the reality of unification; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:8: And proof that the closeness and unity of the sefirot come from the side of Chesed is that the 248 positive commandments come from the side of Chesed, as explained in the Tikkunim, whose words we will copy below; and every commandment [mitzvah] is a unification of all of Atzilut, which is YHVH - and it is already explained in the Tikkunim (73a) and in the Ra'aya Meheimna (see Pinchas 228b) that "mitzvah" is literally YHVH, for "MTZ" [in At-Bash cipher] is Y-H, and the term "mitzvot" means unification - along the lines of (Berachot 6b), "the whole world was created only to keep this one company [tzavta]" - and this is Eloah, called Chesed, as explained in Parashat Vayikra (23b), and likewise in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar) that Chesed unifies vav-heh. And along these lines, "by day the LORD commands [yetzaveh] His kindness [chasdo]" (Psalms 42:9) - Chesed is called "yoma" [day], which includes all the days, and Chesed builds with them all and unifies them - along the lines of (ibid. 89:3), "I have said, the world is built with kindness [chesed]." And this is what it says there, "crowned with Chesed on every side" - meaning in every direction, and "everything is done with Chesed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:9: And so too it says, in this very passage, concerning the matter of the four compartments of the tefillin (Zohar, Va'etchanan 262b), in these words: the third [compartment]: "Shema Yisrael" - Yisrael Sava; "and you shall love the LORD your God" - Rabbi Shimon taught, this is the supernal secret: Israel is crowned on the side of Abba, and what is that? Abraham; and it is crowned on the side of Imma, and what is that? Isaac. We have learned, "and you shall love" - because he loves the King, he does extra kindness with everyone; and this extra kindness is called "chesed shel emet" [true kindness], which requires no reward for it, but only because of the King's love, that He loves him more; and on the King's love depends Chesed, and this is the third compartment - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:10: Behold, it is explained that the lover causes the spread of Chesed in the world, as he writes, "and because he loves Him more, Chesed increases in the world." Indeed, what he said, that "Israel is crowned on the side of Abba," may be understood together with what is explained in the Idra of Ha'azinu (291a), concerning the two crowns that were hidden in Abba and Imma, and they crowned him with them. And it is possible that he brought this matter here to explain the phrase "YHVH your God [Elohecha]" - for YHVH is called from the side of the crown of Abba, and "Elohecha" from the side of the crown of Imma. Or it is possible that the crowns are alluded to in the extra word "et" [the direct-object particle in "et YHVH Elohecha"], and the first explanation seems to me primary - and "et" is the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:11: And what he said, that true service in the matter of love is one who does not serve in order to receive a reward, and this one merits Chesed - the reason is that one who serves in order to receive a reward is necessarily bound to the side of Gevurah, for according to the measure of his service, he is flowed to according to strict judgment and precise reckoning. But one who serves not in order to receive a reward - since his service is without measure, in that he does not wait for a known portion of reward - so too he is given without measure from the side of Chesed, for Chesed flows without measure, and then he is bound in love. And therefore, since he does not serve in order to receive a reward, but rather from complete love, he causes the crown of Gevurah to be included beneath the crown of Chesed, and the acts of kindness spread to all the extremities - for Chesed is what spreads in the world, and the entire building of the world is with Chesed, without any prior kindness [owed], but rather it is His way of goodness to do good and give both to the evil and to the good, without being exacting with any creature; and it is the way of the attribute of Chesed to love, to give, and to desire - for from the love it has for the caused things and all creatures, it flows its kindness to them, without having received from them any arousal for which it flows to them. So too, one who loves the King performs kindness with the King - and the kindness is to perform service and not hope for the reward of the service, corresponding to the attribute of Chesed - and thereby he is bound to the attribute of Chesed and "Chesed increases."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:12: And he explained, in brief words, the matter of love, when he said, "but only because of the King's love, that He loves him more" - the intent is that love of the King is so fixed in his heart that there is nothing in the world he loves more than the King; and this is "that He loves him more" - more than all the things in the world - and therefore he does not serve in order to receive a reward, for [otherwise] he would be found serving and loving for the sake of the reward, and not from the side of love of the King. And even if he loves both the reward and the King, even so it is not fitting that any reward be considered equal to the love of the King, in such a way that no created thing in the world - even the reward of the World to Come - should be found that he loves more than the Holy One, blessed be He; rather, the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, exceeds everything - and therefore the merit of one who serves in this manner is rewarded without measure or limit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:13: As is explained (Zohar, Va'etchanan 267a), in these words: "and you shall love" - whoever loves the Holy One, blessed be He, and is crowned with Chesed on every side, and performs kindness in everything, and does not spare his body or his wealth - from where do we derive this? From Abraham, as it is said, for in his love of his Master he did not spare his heart (which is his inclination), nor his soul, nor his wealth. "His heart" - he did not attend to his own will because of his love of his Master. "His soul, his son, and his wife" - because of his love of his Master. "His wealth" - for he stood at the crossroads and prepared food for the whole world; because of this he was crowned with the crown of Chesed, as it is written (Micah 7:20), "kindness to Abraham" - and whoever binds himself in love of his Master merits this; and not only that, but all the worlds are blessed for his sake - this is what is written (Psalms 145:10), "and Your pious ones shall bless You" - do not read "yevarechucha" [shall bless You] but "yevarchu Koh" [shall bless the letters Koh, i.e., yud-heh].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:14: One day, Rabbi Yosi fell ill; Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Yitzchak, and Rabbi Yehuda came in to him. They saw him fall on his face and sleep. They sat down; when he awoke, they saw his face laughing. Rabbi Abba said to him: have you seen something new? He said to him: certainly - for now my soul ascended and saw the glory of those who gave themselves over for the sanctification of their Master, who were entering the thirteen mountains of pure balsam, and the Holy One, blessed be He, delighted in them; and I saw what I was not given permission to say, and I asked them, whose is this glory? They told me, of those who love their Master in that world - and from what I saw, my soul and heart were illuminated, and therefore my face is laughing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:15: Rabbi Abba said to him: happy is your portion! But the Torah testifies concerning them, as it is written (Isaiah 64:3), "the eye has not seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for one who waits for Him." Rabbi Yehuda said to him: the colleagues have already asked about this - it is written "will do" [ya'aseh], whereas it should have said "will do" [ta'aseh, in a different form implying it applies to God's actions in a specific tense]. He said to him: this has already been stated, but the secret of the matter is what is written (Psalms 27:4), "to gaze upon the pleasantness [no'am] of the LORD and to visit His Heichal" - and they have established that "the pleasantness of the LORD" is that which comes from the holy Ancient One [Atika Kadisha], with which the Holy One, blessed be He, delights, for that pleasantness comes from the Ancient One. Here too, "the eye has not seen, O God, besides You, what He will do" - who is this? The concealed, Ancient One of all, upon whom everything depends. He said to him: certainly, so it is. Happy is the portion of those who cleave to the love of their Master - for these, there is no measure to their portion in that world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:16: Rabbi Yitzchak said: how many compartments upon compartments the righteous have in that world, and the uppermost compartment of all is for those bound in the love of their Master - for their compartment is bound to everything and ascends above everything. Why so? Because the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned by this - come and see, everything is called "love," and so on - copied at the beginning of this chapter - to this point. Behold, it is explained, concerning the virtue of one who serves out of love, that he merits the supernal pleasantness that "no eye has seen."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:17: And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, a more explained reason for the virtue of one who serves out of love: that one who serves out of love of the King of the world, not in hope of reward in this world, nor in hope of reward in the World to Come, but only out of love - the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself pays his reward. For if one does it for the sake of reward in this world, so that he have wealth and children, behold, he receives his reward in this world; and just as this world decays and perishes in this world, so his reward decays and perishes in this world. And if he does it for the sake of the Garden of Eden, his reward comes through the world of the angels who serve the Garden; but if he does it out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He, he attaches his soul to the Infinite and to His attributes, to unify them properly, and therefore his reward is from above the above, "to gaze upon the pleasantness of the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:18: And it appears to me, in further explaining this matter, that each person merits, in the future, according to his deeds: if he merited [the level of] the nefesh alone, his rest is in the place of the souls, in the courtyard of death; if he merited the ruach, he merits the Garden of Eden; and if he merited the neshamah, he merits to ascend to the supernal Garden of Eden - and those who merit the neshamah are called "lovers," as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Vayigash 206a), on "to cause those who love Me to inherit substance [yesh]" (Proverbs 8:21) - these are the ones in whom the holy neshamah is; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:19: And what he wrote, "for their compartment is bound to everything" - meaning, every single compartment in the Garden of Eden nurses from a particular attribute and is bound to that attribute according to the commandment he performed; but the compartment of the pious is a compartment that nurses from all of Atzilut and is bound to all of it, for the reason that he caused all of Atzilut to be unified, as explained - and "ascends above everything" means that the reality of this compartment is above all the other compartments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:20: And the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, wrote on the Mishnah (Avot 1:3), "do not be like servants who serve on condition of receiving a reward," and likewise on the Mishnah (ibid. 5:16), "any love that is dependent on something," matters pertaining to love, and I have therefore seen fit to copy some of them, those necessary for the subject we are engaged in.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:21: He wrote on the Mishnah "do not be like," in these words: our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 50b): it is written (Psalms 57:11), "for Your kindness is great, reaching to the heavens," and it is written (ibid. 108:5), "for Your kindness is great above the heavens" - this is not difficult: here it refers to those who act for their [commandments'] own sake, and so on - for one who acts for its own sake cleaves to the Blessed Name, and there is no limit to the giving of his reward; but those who believe in the Blessed Name, that He rewards and punishes, and occupy themselves with His commandments even more - their reward is fixed, reaching to the heavens. And know that the great and awesome day of the LORD is above the heavens, and the discerning will understand. And to this King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:159), "see how I have loved Your precepts; O LORD, revive me according to Your kindness" - for I am among those who act for their own sake, therefore I ask from a treasury that has no limit, which is Your great kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:22: And to this the prophet said (Lamentations 3:21), "this I recall to my mind, therefore I have hope. The kindnesses of the LORD, that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not; they are new every morning, great is Your faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, says my soul, therefore will I hope in Him." And we must explain what is "this," which he recalled to his mind, and what his soul said. And the matter, in my view, is that a person, insofar as he is [merely] human, finds it hard to conceive of service on condition of not receiving reward, and this is possible only for the soul, from the side of its own nature - for it is from the supernal realms and desires, by nature, His service, like the angels above; and people whose humanity has become entirely soul-like are the ones who serve on condition of not receiving reward. And to this he said, that to his heart, in what is human about it, he said things that settle in the heart; but to his soul he need not say arguments, for it itself will say that it chooses service for its own sake and not for the sake of anything else - and this is his saying (ibid. 3:24), "the LORD is my portion, says my soul, therefore I will hope in Him" - from a different argument.
